open-question.question: The answer sweep today runs its own lift call for each question before recording it, using the call's failure as the per-question skip and its printed line as the commit body, and the answer-with-recommendation procedure it then follows runs the same lift again in its own step 2. With the sweep inline and that procedure's contract now open to change, should the sweep drop its separate lift and use the procedure's own lift instead (its failure treated as the per-question skip, its printed line held as the commit body), or keep a separate lift before following the procedure, so each question is lifted twice?
open-question.alternative: The sweep drops its own lift call and follows answer-with-recommendation-procedure.md from its lift step. The sweep treats a failure of that procedure's lift as the per-question skip and keeps the line that lift prints as the commit body. This is the same way the single-question answer-open-question-with-recommendation skill already keeps the procedure's lift print for its commit. Each question is lifted exactly once. The inline sweep and the single-question skill then run the procedure the same way, so the lift that re-checks the question, gates the skip and supplies the body is also the lift that feeds the recorded ANSWER and RECORDED OPTION. The two can never drift apart. The procedure's no-recommendation guard currently says to stop and report the tool's Error: line, but the sweep needs a silent skip that moves on. So either the procedure's guard wording or the sweep's text has to separate a lift failure, which is a skip, from any later failure after the fold, which stops the whole run. That boundary then sits inside a shared file that the single-question skill also follows.

The sweep keeps its own lift call per question as the re-check, skip and commit-body source, and only then follows answer-with-recommendation-procedure.md unchanged. The procedure lifts the same block a second time in its own step. The procedure's contract and its stop-on-failed-lift guard stay exactly as they are. The skip decision is made before the procedure starts, so the procedure's guard can never fire inside the sweep. The sweep's per-question structure also stays what the CLAUDE.md sweep invariant describes today: the lift call itself is the re-check. Every question costs a redundant tool call and a second read of the lifted line. Both lifts must be described in the skill, which duplicates prose. The sweep has to make clear which print it keeps as the body, even though nothing writes between the two calls so they cannot differ.

The sweep keeps its own single lift as re-check, skip and body source. It skips answer-with-recommendation-procedure.md and hands the lifted line as ANSWER, plus the text before the first spaced em dash as RECORDED OPTION, straight to the recording core, answer-procedure.md. One lift per question, and neither shared procedure's contract changes. The sweep controls the skip-versus-stop boundary in its own text, and the recording core already accepts a caller-supplied ANSWER and RECORDED OPTION. The goal says the sweep runs the shared answer-with-recommendation procedure itself, so the goal would need rewording. The derivation of RECORDED OPTION from the lifted line would be written out in two places. And once the sweep leaves, answer-with-recommendation-procedure.md has only one runner, the single-question skill, which conflicts with the project rule that a shared file needs two or more runners and would push the procedure toward being inlined.

answer-with-recommendation-procedure.md gains an optional pre-lifted ANSWER input. The sweep lifts once itself, for the re-check, skip and body, and passes that line in. The procedure runs its own lift only when the line is not supplied, as in the single-question skill. One lift per question. The sweep still formally follows the shared procedure as the goal says, and the skip stays decided in the sweep before the procedure starts. The procedure would branch on whether an input was supplied. The recorded milestone-resolution decision rules that pattern out for MILESTONE_DIR ("neither procedure branches on whether the input was supplied"). It also adds a second path through a shared file for a saving of one cheap tool call per question.

open-question.question: The goal still describes an end-of-run check in which a walk call's print is reported as the still-skipped advisory, while the recorded skipped-question decision has the sweep name no skipped question and add no end-of-run call to find them. Does the inline sweep keep any end-of-run walk call at all, and if it does not, is the goal's end-of-run sentence to be revised so the two documents agree?

The goal says a contradiction the sweep happens to notice is reported once beside the terse status line while the run proceeds, but not what counts as one or what the advisory carries. Does a contradiction cover only a pick against an entry already under Decisions, or also a pick against a decision the same run recorded earlier and a pick against another standing pick, and does the advisory name the Short Titles and decisions involved or stay identifier-free?

The headless-chain decision lands the page edit only after a confirming run of the new fable-high sweep settings on this repository, but the inline sweep exists only once this milestone's tasks are complete, by which time this milestone's own questions are already answered. Which run counts as the confirming run, and does the documentation task wait within this milestone for a later milestone's first sweep or land on some other confirmation?
